claims.text: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni can be processed into a single-phase FCC initial state.
Mechanical-behavior variations among single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are primarily governed by changes in local lattice distortion.
Changes in local lattice distortion alter stacking-fault energy.
Stacking-fault energy controls the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Stacking-fault-energy changes affect the ease of dislocation cross-slip.
Reducing or rearranging the constituent elements changes the effective atomic-size mismatch.
Changes in effective atomic-size mismatch produce different degrees of local lattice distortion.
Greater local lattice distortion lowers the propensity for deformation-twin formation.
Greater local lattice distortion alters dislocation mobility and enhances dislocation pinning.
Quaternary and ternary subsets with greater local lattice distortion will have higher yield strength than the equiatomic quinary alloy.
Quaternary and ternary subsets with greater local lattice distortion will have lower ductility than the equiatomic quinary alloy.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline exhibits a balance between dislocation slip and twinning that produces a strength-ductility trade-off.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase FCC alloys processed under similar thermomechanical conditions.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply when compositional changes introduce secondary phases or when processing conditions differ drastically.
